main_text.p: quis enim senserunt cum Seleucianis) censetur, Christum in carne non venisse. Id quod aperte Antichristianum dogma vocat Ioannes 1. epi-stola, cap.4.vers.3. & totum salutis nostrae fun-damentum subruit, denique Deum mendacem constituit, & efficit falsam Euangelij praedica-tionem. Itaque plane blasphema sententia dicenda est. His autem simillimę fuerunt aliquę duę haereticorum familiae, quorum Ioan. Damascenus meminit. Ex iis autę alij Christolytæ (quod Christum dissoluerent, & Christum cum carne in coelum ascendisse negent) alij Aphtartodoci-tæ nominantur, quod Christum verum hom-inem fuisse negent, & vere passum, nostrisque infirmitatibus, excepto tamen peccato, corpus obnoxium assumpsisse. Quæ omnes sententiæ plane nostram salutem evertunt, & sunt repeti-ta Marcionitarum crambe.
main_text.head: CAP. LXI.
Patriciani cur sic appellati. Erroris eorum capita duo recensentur.

p.i: Patriciani{1} a Patricio nuncupati, substantiam carnis humanæ non a Deo, sed a diabolo conditam dicunt, eamque sic fingendam & detestandam putant, ut quidam eorum perhibeantur etiam morte sibi illata carere carne voluisse.

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a P, joined to "atriciani" as "Patriciani". The superscript "2" after "carnis" has no matching note on this page. The word "hom-inem" is split at the line end; the hyphen is printed, but the second part is read as "inem" with the line beginning "nem", so the split is uncertain. The word "simillimę" and "aliquę" carry printed ligatures/cedillas that are read as ę and ę and may need checking. The foot note is continued in the last line of the page, which ends with "&" and no catchword.
